Class GeoMesaColumnCatalog

java.lang.Object
org.locationtech.geomesa.trino.spatial.iceberg.GeoMesaColumnCatalog
public final class GeoMesaColumnCatalog extends Object
Shared per-connector cache of GeometryColumn descriptors, keyed by SchemaTableName. Owned by SpatialConnector; populated lazily by SpatialConnectorMetadata (which has access to the delegate ConnectorMetadata.getColumnHandles) and read back by it during applyFilter.

Discovery: a VARBINARY column X becomes a GeometryColumn iff at least one of __X_bbox__, __X_z2__, __X_xz2__ exists in the same table's column map.

Cache lifecycle: lazy population with a 5-minute expire-after-write TTL, so companion-column DDL is picked up without a restart. Staleness in either direction is prune-safe. DDL forwarded through the spatial connector invalidates eagerly (invalidate(SchemaTableName)/ invalidateSchema(String)); tables dropped outside it (plain iceberg catalog, REST API, maintenance tools) simply expire. Expiry is safe on both caches: geometry descriptors re-discover on the next resolve(SchemaTableName, ConnectorSession, ConnectorTableHandle, ConnectorMetadata), and the visibility record is re-written at analysis time (before the access control reads it) on every query, with fail-closed semantics if it is ever absent. The visibility cache uses a longer retention so an entry never expires between the analysis-time write and the same query's row-filter read.

    • invalidate

      public void invalidate(io.trino.spi.connector.SchemaTableName tableName)
      Drops all cached state for a table. Called when forwarded DDL removes or renames it, so a later table at the same name re-discovers its geometry and visibility columns instead of being served stale descriptors.
      Parameters:
      tableName - the schema-qualified table name
